title: fix(plugin-detail): record:details edit mode edits a textarea field in a multi-line textarea (objectui#11562)
body:
Fixes #11562
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`record:details` edit mode now edits a `textarea` field in the fields package's multi-line `TextAreaField`, so a save keeps the line breaks the value was stored with.

- `packages/plugin-detail/src/InlineFieldInput.tsx`: `textarea` leaves `INLINE_PLAIN_TEXT_FIELD_TYPES` (class D, objectui#4220) and joins `INLINE_ROUTED_FIELD_TYPES`. It takes the branch `markdown` got in objectui#11541, which renders `TextAreaField`. The set's docblock drops the warning objectui#11541 wrote about `textarea`. Its "nothing is lost" sentence now covers only the single-line members left: `text`, `email`, `phone`, `url`.
- Drift guard `inlineEditTypeCoverage.test.tsx`: `textarea` moves from `benign` to `routed`. The benign bucket's wording now says single-line.
- `InlineFieldInput.delegation.test.tsx`: `textarea` leaves the class-D loop. The class-D pins for `text`, `email`, `url` and `phone` are unchanged and green.
- New pin file `InlineFieldInput.textareaEditor-11562.test.tsx`.
- One `@object-ui/plugin-detail` patch changeset.

## Deviation from the ruling's mechanism words: `DETAIL_ROUTED_INLINE_TYPES` is untouched

The ruling reads "Route `textarea` through `DETAIL_ROUTED_INLINE_TYPES` to the fields package's multi-line `TextAreaField`". The PR does not add `textarea` to that set. Measured, it is the wrong lever for this type:

- `DETAIL_ROUTED_INLINE_TYPES` exists only to exempt members of the fields package's shared `INLINE_EXCLUDED_FIELD_TYPES` from the detail hosts' gate. `markdown` needed it because `markdown` is in that set. `textarea` is not (`EDIT_WIDGETS` maps it to `TextAreaField`), so both hosts already opened an editor for it. On `origin/main` the pin "the details body shows the inline-edit affordance on a textarea row" is green, and the row in edit mode renders exactly one editor: the one-line terminal input.
- Adding it anyway is refused by an existing pin. Probe leg D below: with `textarea` in `DETAIL_ROUTED_INLINE_TYPES`, `inlineCredentialGate.test.tsx` fails "every exempted type is a member of the shared exclusion (no free-floating entries)" with "textarea must be in the shared set". Nothing else changes.

The substance of the ruling lands as written. The row routes `textarea` to `TextAreaField`, and the drift guard moves it from "benign" to "routed". The route lives where `markdown`'s editor lives: `INLINE_ROUTED_FIELD_TYPES` and the editor branch.

## The defect, measured

On `origin/main` `072b7e8`, `textarea` edited in the terminal input, an INPUT element of type text. The browser strips line breaks from the value such an input is given. A stored note `"Call back Monday.\n\nBudget approved, needs legal review.\n"` showed as `"Call back Monday.Budget approved, needs legal review."`. One keystroke made that flattened string the value the Save batch wrote.

## Pins

New file `InlineFieldInput.textareaEditor-11562.test.tsx`. The multi-line value has a blank line inside and a trailing newline, and every comparison is byte for byte.

- `InlineFieldInput`: a TEXTAREA seeded with the stored value, never the terminal input. One keystroke appended to what the editor shows emits the stored text plus that keystroke. `autoFocus` lands on it.
- `DetailSection`: the pencil shows on a textarea row. Edit mode renders one editor, seeded byte-identical.
- `HeaderHighlight`: the same editor inside the edit session.
- Save round trip: `InlineEditProvider` + `DetailSection` + `InlineEditSaveBar` over a store-backed `update`. The PATCH body is exactly the edited string, the store holds it, and re-entering edit seeds the editor with it.
- Single-line control: the keystroke pin and the round trip also run with `"Call back Monday."`. Both are green on `origin/main` and after the fix, so a single-line value saves exactly as before.
- Grid cell: `FieldEditWidget`, which `ObjectGrid`'s cell editor delegates to, seeds a TEXTAREA with the multi-line value byte for byte. This PR does not touch that path. The pin records that the row and the cell now edit with one widget.

## Verification

All at `5af2bb9` (the only commit), from the worktree.

- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter "@object-ui/plugin-detail^..." build`: exit 0. 12 projects in scope, all 11 with a build script printed Done (`test-support` has none).
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/plugin-detail/`: Test Files 233 passed, 1 skipped (234). Tests 2313 passed, 8 skipped (2321).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail run type-check`: exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists all three touched test files.
- eslint over the 4 touched source and test files (`--no-inline-config --format json`): 4 files, 0 errors. The three edited files carry the same warning counts as at `072b7e8` (42, 1 and 0, all `no-explicit-any` or `react-refresh`), and the new file carries none. `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions` project, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot change the result for an untouched file.
- `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-test-path-roots`, the three `check-vi-mock-*` checks, `check-unreferenced-sources`, `check-type-check-coverage`, `check-lint-coverage`: all exit 0.

Ablations, after the commit. Each mutation went through objectstack's `ablation-replace.mjs`, or a trap-armed whole-file swap for leg C. Each restore is proven by the blob hash equal to HEAD's and an empty `git diff HEAD`. Each leg ran the new pin file, the drift guard and the delegation suite.

- Leg A, `textarea` put back into `INLINE_PLAIN_TEXT_FIELD_TYPES`: 2 failed, 113 passed. The drift guard's "no type is claimed twice" and its benign-list pin fail. The new pins stay green because the routed branch runs before the class-D test. A first attempt at this leg did not run: the tool refused an anchor that its own replacement contained, and nothing was measured.
- Leg B, only the branch's `textarea` disjunct deleted: green, 115 passed. This direction is the expected one. The type is no longer class D, so it falls to the delegation tail, and `FieldEditWidget` renders the same `TextAreaField`. See the acceptance notes.
- Leg C, `InlineFieldInput.tsx` swapped whole to `072b7e8` (byte-identical to `origin/main`): 9 failed, 106 passed. 7 are in the new pin file: every multi-line pin and every pin on the editor's kind. The 2 single-line controls stay green. The other 2 are in the drift guard.
- Leg D, the ruling's mechanism words: `textarea` added to `DETAIL_ROUTED_INLINE_TYPES` (with `inlineCredentialGate.test.tsx` in the run): 1 failed, 151 passed, as described above.

CI runs the full farm. Locally only `plugin-detail` was run. The plugin-detail sets this PR edits are not exported from the package index, and outside `plugin-detail` no test imports them or queries the terminal input on a `textarea` row.

## Acceptance notes

- Leg B shows that for `textarea` the explicit branch and the delegation tail reach the same widget. So the drift guard cannot tell a routed `textarea` from a delegated one: deleting the branch alone stays green, and the user still gets `TextAreaField`. The branch follows the ruling's "routed" bucket and `markdown`'s precedent. What the pins do guard is the actual regression, `textarea` landing back on the one-line input (leg C, and leg A at the guard).
- The grid's record overlay (`RecordDetailPanel`, which `plugin-grid` imports from this package) renders the same detail hosts, so it gets the multi-line editor too. The grid CELL still edits with `FieldEditWidget`, unchanged.
- `packages/plugin-detail/README.md` is not touched. objectui#11512 edits it, and it does not describe per-type inline editors. No `content/docs` page lists which editor a detail row uses per type, so no guide page changes.
- Reach, from the card: `notes: Field.textarea` on objectstack `examples/app-crm`'s lead and `examples/app-showcase`'s task.
